requirements.evidence: Nearly the whole contract is present: migrations (database/migrations/2026_10_01_000001_create_queues_table.php:14-23, database/migrations/2026_10_01_000002_create_tickets_table.php:14-27), Queue model (app/Models/Queue.php:11-37), Entity::queues() (app/Models/Entity.php:41-44), Ticket model with nextCode/call (app/Models/Ticket.php:80-133), both enums, InactiveQueueException, the action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:25-61) and tests. However database/factories/TicketFactory.php:46 declares `protected function store(Collection $results)`, overriding the public `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\Factory::store()`; PHP rejects the reduced visibility with a fatal error, so the required `Ticket::factory()` (and any test using it) cannot work.

conventions.evidence: Migrations follow the generated stub and have reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_01_000002_create_tickets_table.php:34), fillable/casts are explicit (app/Models/Queue.php:11-27, app/Models/Ticket.php:15-57), domain write goes through app/Actions/IssueTicket.php, docs are updated (docs/business-rules.md Issuance/Display code sections, docs/database-schema.md:156-162), and CHANGELOG.md:12 is under [Unreleased]. security.evidence: Membership is checked server-side before the update (app/Models/Ticket.php:115-118), the ticket is re-read under `lockForUpdate` and its status re-checked (app/Models/Ticket.php:123-127), negative priority is rejected (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27-29), and fillable lists are explicit (app/Models/Queue.php:11, app/Models/Ticket.php:15). No Livewire, uploads or unescaped output in the diff. The only weakness is architectural: authorization is not centralised in a policy (app/Models/Ticket.php:112), and correctness depends on the unverified `User::membershipFor()` helper returning null for non-members.

simplicity.evidence: nextCode (app/Models/Ticket.php:80-101) is a reasonable paged backward scan, but TicketFactory (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:46-55) overrides the framework's internal store() and re-implements persistence (`parent::store(new Collection([$ticket]))` per model) just to assign codes; a normal state/afterMaking hook would be leaner and would not have introduced the visibility error. QueueFactory (database/factories/QueueFactory.php:21-24) is appropriately small.

readability.evidence: Names and method boundaries are clear (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:25-61, app/Models/Ticket.php:80-133), mutable fields are named in a constant (app/Models/Ticket.php:32), and the row-lock intent is commented (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:44-46, app/Models/Ticket.php:121-123). The `break 2` scan in nextCode (app/Models/Ticket.php:90-100) and the store() reimplementation (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:46-55) take a little effort to follow, but nothing is dead or debug code.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: new enums/exception/models/action/migrations/factories/tests plus the required docs updates (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md) and CHANGELOG. The only stray edit is the duplicated CHANGELOG bullet in the released [0.0.0] section (CHANGELOG.md:39).

issues.explanation: `protected function store(Collection $results)` reduces the visibility of the public `Factory::store()` method, which is a PHP fatal error; every `Ticket::factory()` call (including the whole new test suite) will fail, so make the override public (or assign codes in a supported hook) and return/persist through the parent correctly.

`Ticket::call()` depends on `$user->membershipFor((int) $entityId)`, a helper that is not part of the diff; if it does not exist this is a fatal error, and if it does not return null (or a falsy value) for non-members the authorization check silently passes, so verify its contract.
The same feature entry is added under the already released `[0.0.0]` section as well as `[Unreleased]`; historical release notes should not be rewritten.

The call authorization is a hand-rolled membership lookup rather than a policy/gate, although the conventions require authorization to always go through `app/Policies`; the task's `Ticket::call()` contract can still delegate to a `TicketPolicy`.

Models use the newer `#[Fillable]` attribute (also app/Models/Ticket.php:15) instead of the `$fillable` property; the diff does not include composer.json, so the installed Laravel version supporting `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable` cannot be verified, and on an older version the models fall back to guarded-everything and inserts fail.

The test passes priority 10 and `TicketChannel::Totem` but only asserts the resulting code, so custom priority/channel persistence is never verified; the Queue factory's entity creation, the `is_active`/`labels_i18n` casts and the collision-retry path are also untested.

The unchanged write-once note still says only `called_at` and `called_by_user_id` are mutable, contradicting the implementation (and the new note below it) where `status` and `updated_at` are also mutable, so the docs section is internally inconsistent.

review.summary: The change implements the queues/tickets domain core: migrations, models and factories, enums, InactiveQueueException, the row-locked IssueTicket action with collision retry, the write-once guard, member-only single call, tests and the required docs/changelog updates. Most requirements read correctly, but the ticket factory overrides the public Factory::store() as protected, a PHP fatal that breaks the required factory and the whole test suite; the changelog entry is also duplicated under the released version. Overall 3: a solid change that needs the factory fix and a few small follow-ups before merging.
